cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: You Can’t Leave Mid-Prophecy
cards.instruction: Keep someone present until the impossible prediction has been fulfilled, disproved, or responsibly revised.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep your coat off. This bell-less tower is meant to ring at noon, and I need you listening with me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's twelve-oh-one. I'll call the clock office to check, then go.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not while we're listening for the tower. Keep the phone silent. How reliable is your watch?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we have four minutes. Stay here; I'll watch the hands and you listen. Please don't telephone anyone to ask whether you can hear something.

cardFidelity.evidence: A3 corrects the proposed phone call as interference with observation and A5 assigns clock/listening roles to retain B until the real noon.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 call and departure proposal causes A3 reliability check; B4 fast watch yields the correct four-minute wait.

relationship.evidence: B2 seeks independent timing confirmation and B4 provides the watch fault, practical contributions despite A's patronizing reply.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4 exact offset to keep B for a bounded interval and supervise how they listen.

specificity.evidence: A1 bell-less tower and noon ringing make the impossible prediction explicit; B2 watch gives timing stakes.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 final rebuke is a character's unfair simplification of B2 timing call, not a claim that B literally asked others to hear for them.
